proposals.before: His father Yao Yi, courtesy name Shanyi, had served as commissioner of Yi Prefecture during the Zhenguan reign and was posthumously honored as Grand Military Commissioner of You Prefecture with the posthumous name Wenxian.
proposals.after: His father Yao Yi, courtesy name Shanyi, had served as commander-in-chief of Xi Prefecture (巂州) during the Zhenguan reign and was posthumously honored as Grand Commander-in-chief of You Prefecture with the posthumous name Wenxian.
proposals.reason: 巂州 is Xi Prefecture, not Yi; 都督 is commander-in-chief rather than commissioner.

proposals.before: His father Yi, styled Shanyi, in the Zhenguan era served as military commissioner of Yi Prefecture, was posthumously made Grand Military Commissioner of You Prefecture, and given the posthumous title Wenxian.
proposals.after: His father Yi, styled Shanyi, in the Zhenguan era served as commander-in-chief of Xi Prefecture, was posthumously made Grand Commander-in-chief of You Prefecture, and given the posthumous title Wenxian.
proposals.reason: Same 巂州 misread as Yi Prefecture in the literal line.

proposals.before: I thought them wronged, yet feared that when close ministers interrogated them, all obtained their written confessions that they were not wronged; I had no doubts and at once approved their memorials.
proposals.after: I thought them wronged, but when close ministers went to interrogate them they all obtained written confessions that there was no injustice; I had no doubts and at once approved their memorials.
proposals.reason: 更畏近臣臨問 is concessive about the reinvestigations' results, not Wu fearing the ministers themselves.

proposals.before: In the third year of Shenglì he was promoted to associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
proposals.after: In the third year of Shengli he was promoted to joint manager of affairs with the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace (chancellor).
proposals.reason: 同鳳閣鸞臺平章事 is a chancellor title, not an associate directorship of the two departments.

proposals.before: The crown prince was afraid and submitted a memorial accusing Chong and the others of driving a wedge into the royal house, asking that they be punished; they were demoted to Prefect of Shen Prefecture.
proposals.after: The crown prince was afraid and submitted a memorial accusing Chong and the others of driving a wedge into the royal house, asking that they be punished; Chong was demoted to Prefect of Shen Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 貶為申州刺史 is singular; the idiomatic line correctly makes Yao Chong the subject of the demotion.

proposals.before: Empress Wu built the Xian Temple at vast expense, and the Retired Emperor built the Jinxian and Yuzhen abbeys, costing millions;
proposals.after: Empress Wu built Fuxian Temple at vast expense, and the Retired Emperor built the Jinxian and Yuzhen abbeys, costing millions;
proposals.reason: 福先寺 is Fuxian Temple, not Xian Temple.

proposals.before: Empress Wu built blessings at Xian Temple; the Retired Emperor built the two abbeys Jinxian and Yuzhen, costing millions;
proposals.after: Empress Wu built Fuxian Temple; the Retired Emperor built the two abbeys Jinxian and Yuzhen, costing millions;
proposals.reason: 造福先寺 means building Fuxian Temple, not building blessings at Xian Temple.

proposals.before: In Zhongzong's time, close kin memorialized to ordain monks and nuns; warm households and strong young men thereby avoided rent and corvée.
proposals.after: In Zhongzong's time, close kin memorialized to ordain monks and nuns; affluent households and strong young men thereby avoided rent and corvée.
proposals.reason: 溫戶 means well-off registered households, not thermally warm households.

proposals.before: In time Zhao Hui, an assistant in the Bureau of Astronomy, was found to have taken bribes from foreigners and faced execution.
proposals.after: In time Zhao Hui, a clerk of the Purple Forbidden Secretariat, was found to have taken bribes from foreigners and faced execution.
proposals.reason: 紫微史 under Xuanzong is a Zhongshu/Purple Forbidden Secretariat clerk, not an astronomical-bureau post.

proposals.before: After a long while, Assistant in the Bureau of Astronomy Zhao Hui received bribes from barbarians and should die.
proposals.after: After a long while, Zhao Hui, a clerk of the Purple Forbidden Secretariat, received bribes from barbarians and should die.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 紫微史 as astronomy rather than the Purple Forbidden Secretariat.

proposals.before: Fearing for himself, Chong resigned the chancellorship, recommended Song Jing as successor, and was relieved of office with the honorific rank of Defender-in-Chief.
proposals.after: Fearing for himself, Chong resigned the chancellorship, recommended Song Jing as successor, and was relieved of government affairs with the honorific rank of Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is the prestige rank kaifu yitong sansi, not Defender-in-Chief (太尉).

proposals.before: Chong was fearful; he returned the chancellorship, brought in Song Jing to replace him, and was dismissed from government affairs with the title of Defender-in-Chief and Concurrent Supervisor of State Affairs.
proposals.after: Chong was fearful; he returned the chancellorship, brought in Song Jing to replace him, and was dismissed from government affairs with the title Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes.
proposals.reason: 罷政事 with 開府儀同三司 does not mean Defender-in-Chief or concurrent supervisor of state affairs.

proposals.before: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Defender-in-Chief of Yangzhou with the posthumous name Wenxian.
proposals.after: He was posthumously made Grand Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, with the posthumous name Wenxian.
proposals.reason: 揚州大都督 is the Yangzhou area command, not Defender-in-Chief.

proposals.before: He was posthumously made Defender-in-Chief of Yangzhou; his posthumous title was Wenxian (Literary and Illustrious).
proposals.after: He was posthumously made Grand Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou; his posthumous title was Wenxian (Literary and Illustrious).
proposals.reason: Same error: 大都督 is not Defender-in-Chief.

proposals.before: More recently Emperor Xiahe sent agents to buy the release of animals; Princess Taiping, Wu Sansi, and others ordained followers and built temples—yet they were executed and became a laughingstock.
proposals.after: More recently Emperor Xiaohe sent agents to buy the release of animals; Princess Taiping, Wu Sansi, and others ordained followers and built temples—yet they were executed and became a laughingstock.
proposals.reason: 孝和 is Xiaohe, not Xiahe; the temple-name romanization is wrong.

proposals.before: He had three sons—Yi, Yi, and Yi—each rising to ministerial rank or provincial governorship.
proposals.after: He had three sons—Yi (Yí, 彝), Yi (Yì, 異), and Yi (Yì, 弈)—each rising to ministerial rank or provincial governorship.
proposals.reason: The three given names 彝、異、弈 are distinct characters collapsed into identical English Yi.

proposals.before: Yi asked to administer Ju, became prefect of Suiyang, then was recalled and made Grand Master of the Herds.
proposals.after: Yi asked to take on a demanding jurisdiction, became prefect of Suiyang, then was recalled and made Grand Master of the Herds.
proposals.reason: 治劇 means to request a difficult post, not a place named Ju.

proposals.before: He requested to govern Ju, served as prefect of Suiyang, and was summoned and appointed Grand Master of the Herds.
proposals.after: He requested to govern a demanding commandery, served as prefect of Suiyang, and was summoned and appointed Grand Master of the Herds.
proposals.reason: 劇 is a type of post, not the toponym Ju.

proposals.before: While prefect of Tongzhou, he incurred Zhang Shuo's lasting enmity; Shuo induced Zhao Yanzhao to impeach him.
proposals.after: While prefect of Tongzhou, he incurred Zhang Yue's lasting enmity; Yue induced Zhao Yanzhao to impeach him.
proposals.reason: 張說 is the same man later rendered Zhang Yue; Shuo/Yue split the identity in English.

proposals.before: Promoted to Left Bureau Censor-in-Chief, he learned that Zhang Changzong had consulted a fortune-teller; he demanded a full inquiry. The Empress replied, "Yizhi has already told me himself."
proposals.after: Promoted to Left Bureau Censor-in-Chief, he learned that Zhang Changzong had consulted a fortune-teller; he demanded a full inquiry. The Empress replied, "Yizhi and the others have already told me themselves."
proposals.reason: Chinese 易之等 is plural; the idiomatic quotation drops 等 and makes the confession singular.

proposals.before: Her mood softened, and she allowed Yizhi and his brother to be jailed.
proposals.after: Her mood softened, and she allowed Yizhi and the others to be jailed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 易之等 means Yizhi and the others, not specifically his brother alone.

proposals.before: Yizhi had hoped to destroy Jing once he left the capital; foiled, he planned to murder him at his son's wedding.
proposals.after: Yizhi had hoped to destroy Jing once he left the capital; foiled, he planned to murder him at a wedding in Jing's household.
proposals.reason: Chinese 家婚禮 is a household wedding; the English invents a son not named here.

proposals.before: Jing rebuked him: "The crown prince rules openly—the prince of Tang should return to his fief; why meddle in government? Have you forgotten Lü Lu?"
proposals.after: Jing rebuked him: "Rightful sovereign rule has now been restored—the prince should retire to his marquisate; how can he still meddle in court affairs? Have you not seen the affair of Lü Chan and Lü Lu?"
proposals.reason: 復子明辟 is restoration of rightful rule, not the crown prince ruling openly; 王 is Wu Sansi not a prince of Tang; 產、祿 names both men.

proposals.before: In the Zhenguan era, when the Princess of Changle was married, Wei Zheng said one must not add to the Princess of Changle; Taizong gladly accepted, and Empress Wende sent envoys with generous thanks.
proposals.after: In the Zhenguan era, when the Princess of Changle was married, Wei Zheng said one must not add honors as for a Grand Princess; Taizong gladly accepted, and Empress Wende sent envoys with generous thanks.
proposals.reason: Chinese 不可加長公主 contrasts 長樂公主 with 長公主 (Grand Princess), not a second mention of Princess Changle.

proposals.before: If Your Majesty cannot sway the empress, permit at least a first-rank consort's tomb by the mausoleum—four zhang high, which is near the proper measure."
proposals.after: If the empress's feeling cannot be overborne, I request approving the statute for a first-rank attendant at the imperial tomb, a mound four zhang—roughly fitting what is proper."
proposals.reason: 中宮情不可奪 is the empress's feeling, not 'Your Majesty'; 一品陪陵 is the first-rank accompanying-tomb statute.

proposals.before: To punish lenders for knowing would imply they should have refused—and that would brand refusal as aiding the rebel.
proposals.after: If they had known and still refused to lend, that would have been to side with rebellion.
proposals.reason: 使知而不假，是與為反 means knowing and not lending would count as joining the rebels, not that refusal brands the lenders.

proposals.before: After the Shengli era Moqi chou of the Turks, counting on strength, raided the frontier and attacked the Bayegu of the Nine Surnames; emboldened by victory he rode out carelessly, was ambushed and killed, and frontier envoy Hao Lingjian brought his head to the capital.
proposals.after: After the Shengli era Mo Chuo of the Türks, counting on strength, raided the frontier and attacked the Bayegu of the Nine Surnames; emboldened by victory he rode out carelessly, was ambushed and killed, and the envoy to the frontier Hao Lingquan brought his head to the capital.
proposals.reason: 郝靈亻 is a broken 郝靈佺 (Lingqian/Lingquan in the next sentences); Hao Lingjian mismatches the following English Lingqian.

proposals.before: His son Sheng rose to Vice Minister of the Stud.
proposals.after: His son Sheng was Vice Minister of the Stud.
proposals.reason: Chinese 子升，升，太僕少卿 names Sheng and then his office; 'Sheng rose' invents a verb from a duplicated 升.

proposals.before: His son Hun, close to Li Linfu, served as Remonstrating Censor, Administrator of Pingyuan, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Eastern Capital commissioner.
proposals.after: His son Hun, close to Li Linfu, successively served as Grand Master of Remonstrance, Administrator of Pingyuan, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Eastern Capital Investigating Commissioner.
proposals.reason: 子渾，渾 duplicates the name; 諫議大夫 is Grand Master of Remonstrance, not Remonstrating Censor.

decisions.after: His father Yao Yi, courtesy name Shanyi, had served as commander-in-chief of Xi Prefecture during the Zhenguan reign and was posthumously honored as Grand Commander-in-chief of You Prefecture with the posthumous name Wenxian.
decisions.reason: 巂州 is Xi Prefecture, not Yi Prefecture, and 都督/大都督 are commander-in-chief titles, not commissioner. The proposed parenthesis with the Chinese toponym cannot stand in the English field, so the same correction is kept without the graph.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 為巂州都督，贈幽州大都督

decisions.reason: The literal line repeats the same misreading of 巂州 as Yi and of 都督 as military commissioner.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 為巂州都督，贈幽州大都督

decisions.reason: The original treats 畏 as Wu fearing the ministers; the clause reports that close ministers' interrogations produced written statements of no injustice, after which she approved.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 更畏近臣臨問，皆得其手牒不冤

decisions.reason: 同鳳閣鸞台平章事 is the Wu-Zhou chancellor formula tong pingzhangshi, not an associate directorship of the two departments; 平章事 is omitted in the original.
貶為申州刺史 is grammatically singular and the following transfers (徐、潞、揚州) continue Yao Chong alone, so 'they were demoted' is a subject error.
福先寺 is the temple name Fuxian; 'Xian Temple' drops 福.
造福先寺 is building Fuxian Temple, not 'building blessings at Xian Temple'.
溫戶 are well-off registered households, not thermally warm households.
紫微史 is a clerk of the Purple Forbidden (Zhongshu) Secretariat under Xuanzong, not a Bureau of Astronomy post; 紫微令 in the same chapter names that secretariat.
The literal line makes the same astronomy error for 紫微史.
開府儀同三司 is the prestige rank Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes; 罷政事 is relief from government affairs, not appointment as Defender-in-Chief (太尉).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃以開府儀同三司罷政事

decisions.reason: The original invents Defender-in-Chief and Concurrent Supervisor of State Affairs; the Chinese only grants 開府儀同三司 on dismissal from 政事.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃以開府儀同三司罷政事

decisions.reason: 贈揚州大都督 is a posthumous grand area-command title, not enfeoffment as Defender-in-Chief.
The literal line likewise renders 大都督 as Defender-in-Chief.
孝和 is Xiaohe (Zhongzong's posthumous designation); Xiahe is a wrong romanization.

decisions.after: He had three sons—Yi (Yí), Yi (Yì, 'different'), and Yi (Yì, 'chess')—each rising to ministerial rank or provincial governorship.
decisions.reason: The three given names 彝、異、弈 are distinct and must not be collapsed to identical unmarked Yi; the proposed character glosses cannot stand in the English field, so tone marks and brief English senses disambiguate them.
請治劇 is a request for a demanding jurisdiction, not a toponym Ju.
劇 names a class of difficult post, not a place Ju; 睢陽 is the prefecture that follows.
張說 here is the statesman conventionally Zhang Yue; reading 說 as Shuo splits the same person from later Yue.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 張說以素憾，諷趙彥昭劾崇

decisions.reason: 易之等 is plural; dropping 等 makes the empress's quotation a singular confession by Yizhi alone.
許收易之等就獄 is 'Yizhi and the others'; 'his brother' over-specifies 等.
家婚禮 is a wedding in Jing's household; the original invents a son not named in this sentence.
復子明辟 is restoration of rightful sovereign rule, not the crown prince ruling openly; 王 addresses Wu Sansi, not a prince of Tang; 產、祿 are Lü Chan and Lü Lu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 今復子明辟，王宜以侯就第……獨不見產、祿事乎

decisions.reason: 不可加長公主 contrasts 長樂公主 with the higher rank 長公主 (Grand Princess), not a second mention of Princess Changle.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 嫁長樂公主，魏徵謂不可加長公主

decisions.after: If the empress's feeling cannot be overborne, I request approving the statute for a first-rank accompanying burial at the imperial tomb, a mound four zhang—roughly fitting what is proper."
decisions.reason: 中宮情不可奪 is the empress's feeling, not 'Your Majesty'; 一品陪陵 is the first-rank accompanying-mausoleum statute, not a consort's or attendant's tomb. The proposal fixes the agent but still misrenders 陪陵.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 儻中宮情不可奪，請准令一品陪陵，墳四丈

decisions.reason: 使知而不假，是與為反 is a counterfactual: knowing the plot and refusing to lend would have been siding with rebellion.
默啜 is Mo Chuo, not Moqi chou. The unit's 郝靈亻 is a broken 郝靈佺: Wikisource juan 124 has the same truncated graph, immediately completed as 靈佺, and the parallel Xin Tangshu account writes 郝靈佺 in full.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃與入蕃使郝靈佺傳首京師

decisions.reason: 子升，升，太僕少卿 restates the name 升 then the office; treating the second 升 as the verb 'rose' is an extraction artifact.
諫議大夫 is Grand Master of Remonstrance, not Remonstrating Censor; 東京採訪使 is Eastern Capital Investigating Commissioner; 曆/歷 marks successive tenure.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 曆諫議大夫、平原太守、御史中丞、東京採訪使

claimRevisions.reason: The accepted repair restores the pinyin Xiaohe for 孝和; the extracted English Xiahe was produced only by the bad romanization.
Same Xiaohe restoration in the parallel title-name extraction.
The accepted repair identifies 張說 as Zhang Yue; the extracted personal-name Shuo was the nonstandard reading that split the person.
The given-name extraction must follow the same Yue reading of 說.
默啜 is Mo Chuo; the extracted English Moqi chou was created by the bad translation.
郝靈亻 is a truncated 郝靈佺; Hao Lingjian is not a source name. The person remains the envoy Hao Lingquan attested in the following sentences and in the Xin Tangshu Türk account.
諫議大夫 is Grand Master of Remonstrance; Remonstrating Censor was an office mistranslation in the repaired sentence.
東京採訪使 is the investigating-commissioner title, not a generic Eastern Capital commissioner.
